translations.source_sense_description: zich ergens (met de voeten) op begeven

glosses: An advance or movement made from one foot to the other; a pace.

examples.text: Turning back, then, toward the basement staircase, she began to grope her way through blinding darkness, but had taken only a few uncertain steps when, of a sudden, she stopped short and for a little stood like a stricken thing, quite motionless save that she quaked to her very marrow in the grasp of a great and enervating fear.

glosses: A rest, or one of a set of rests, for the foot in ascending or descending, as a stair, or a rung of a ladder.

examples.text: The breadth of every single step or stair should be never less than one foot.

One morning I had been driven to the precarious refuge afforded by the steps of the inn, after rejecting offers from the Celebrity to join him in a variety of amusements. But even here I was not free from interruption, for he was seated on a horse-block below me, playing with a fox terrier.
Through the open front door ran Jessamy, down the steps to where Kitto was sitting at the bottom with the pram beside him.

glosses: The part of a spade, digging stick or similar tool that a digger's foot rests against and presses on when digging; an ear, a foot-rest.
The button joining a glass's stem to its foot.
A distinct part of a process; stage; phase.

examples.text: He improved step by step, or by steps.
The first step is to find a job.

glosses: A running board where passengers step to get on and off the bus.

examples.text: The driver must have a clear view of the step in order to prevent accidents.

glosses: The space passed over by one movement of the foot in walking or running.

examples.text: One step is generally about three feet, but may be more or less.

To derive two or three general principles of motion from phenomena, and afterwards to tell us how the properties and actions of all corporeal things follow from those manifest principles, would be a very great step in philosophy.

glosses: A small space or distance.

examples.text: It is but a step.

glosses: A print of the foot; a footstep; a footprint; track.
A gait; manner of walking.

examples.text: The approach of a man is often known by his step.
Warwick passed through one of the wide brick arches and traversed the building with a leisurely step.

glosses: Proceeding; measure; action; act.

examples.text: The reputation of a man depends on the first steps he makes in the world.
Beware of desperate steps. The darkest day, Live till to-morrow, will have passed away.
I have lately taken steps[…]to relieve the old gentleman's distresses.
Moon has also requested that government officials take additional steps to help fight pollution, his spokesman said.

glosses: A walk; passage.

examples.text: Conduct my steps to find the fatal tree.

glosses: A portable framework of stairs, much used indoors in reaching to a high position.
A framing in wood or iron which is intended to receive an upright shaft; specifically, a block of wood, or a solid platform upon the keelson, supporting the heel of the mast.
One of a series of offsets, or parts, resembling the steps of stairs, as one of the series of parts of a cone pulley on which the belt runs.
A bearing in which the lower extremity of a spindle or a vertical shaft revolves.
The interval between two contiguous degrees of the scale.

examples.text: Usage note: The word tone is often used as the name of this interval; but there is evident incongruity in using tone for indicating the interval between tones. As the word scale is derived from the Italian scala, a ladder, the intervals may well be called steps.

glosses: A change of position effected by a motion of translation.

examples.text: A change of position effected by a motion of translation will be called a step.

glosses: A constant difference between consecutive values in a series.

examples.text: Printing from 0 to 9 with a step of 3 will display 0, 3, 6 and 9.

glosses: Kick scooter.
Stepping (style of dance)
To move the foot in walking; to advance or recede by raising and moving one of the feet to another resting place, or by moving both feet in succession.

examples.text: A “moving platform” scheme[…]is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails. Local trains would use side-by-side rails to roll alongside intercity trains and allow passengers to switch trains by stepping through docking bays.

glosses: To walk; to go on foot; especially, to walk a little distance.

examples.text: to step to one of the neighbors
Some days later it happened that young Heriotside was stepping home over the Lang Muir about ten at night, it being his first jaunt from home since his arm had mended.
Well... It's hard to talk about in front of the children. Can we step outside?

glosses: To walk slowly, gravely, or resolutely.

examples.text: Home from his Morning-Task , the Swain retreats, His flock before him stepping to the fold.

glosses: To dance.

examples.text: At arms length with left hands clasped they moved back where facing each other they stepped in time to their dance embrace.

She clapped, but instead of walking her back to the table, Alex took her hand and pulled her gently towards him, slipping his arm around her waist again and stepping her off on the first beat of the next dance.
He stepped to the beat of one of their favorite songs.
He put on a tame version of the 1960s song “The Letter,” wrapped his right arm around my waist, raised my right hand, draped it over his left, and we stepped, stepped, and back stepped to the beat.

glosses: To move mentally; to go in imagination.

examples.text: They are stepping almost three thousand years back into the remotest antiquity.

glosses: To set, as the foot.

examples.text: One of the women, Elsie, stepped her foot inside to help the woman.

glosses: To fix the foot of (a mast) in its step; to erect.

examples.text: We put everything straight, stepped the long-boat's mast for our skipper, who was in charge of her, and I was not sorry to sit down for a moment.

glosses: To advance a process gradually, one step at a time.
To depart.

examples.text: You best step, cuz things are about to jump off.

glosses: To be confrontational.

examples.text: You tryna be steppin right now? You better bring it if so.

glosses: A stepchild.

examples.text:

 [Woman:] Step – but well brung up.

glosses: A stepsibling.

examples.text: So for Richard and Barbara, Jeff and Kari, the impossibly varied collection of steps and halves that is another legacy of my father.

glosses: To go or come into (a state or profession).

examples.text: My twelve-year-old son will be entering his teens next year.

glosses: To type (something) into a computer; to input.

examples.text: Enter your user name and password.

glosses: To record (something) in an account, ledger, etc.

examples.text: Each amount entered in the debit column of the journal is posted by entering it on the credit side/column of an account in the ledger.

glosses: To become a party to an agreement, treaty, etc.

examples.text: I am pleased to notify the Congress of my intent to enter into a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) with the Government of Singapore.

glosses: To become effective; to come into effect.

examples.text: This Act shall enter into force on 01 March 1998.

glosses: To go into or upon, as lands, and take actual possession of them.
To place in regular form before the court, usually in writing; to put upon record in proper from and order

examples.text: to enter a writ, appearance, rule, or judgment

glosses: To make report of (a vessel or its cargo) at the custom house; to submit a statement of (imported goods), with the original invoices, to the proper customs officer for estimating the duties. See entry.
To file, or register with the land office, the required particulars concerning (a quantity of public land) in order to entitle a person to a right of preemption.

examples.text: Under existing laws governing the qualifications of an alien to enter 160 acres or more of the public domain he is only required to file his declaration of intent to become a citizen.

glosses: To deposit for copyright the title or description of (a book, picture, map, etc.).

examples.text: entered according to act of Congress

glosses: To initiate; to introduce favourably.

examples.text: This sword but shown to Caesar, with this tidings, / Shall enter me with him.

glosses: To begin (a regular activity or job); to undertake; to take up.

examples.text: […] I entered, that same day, on a regular occupation of pushing Miss Havisham in this chair […] round her own room, and across the landing, and round the other room.

examples.text:

examples.text:

examples.text:
